title: On-call and Incident Response Playbook
author: Ava Chen
content:
Overview

Purpose:
This playbook documents Redwood Inference's standard process for on-call rotations, incident detection and escalation, runbook procedures for common failure modes, postmortem expectations, game day exercises, and status page / customer communications templates. The goal is fast, consistent incident handling that minimizes user impact and enables reliable root-cause analysis and prevention.

Scope:
Applies to all production-facing services (hosted API, Dedicated control plane, Redwood Console, and Private deployment control-plane components). Non-production incidents should follow the same pattern but may use abbreviated comms.

Table of Contents:
1) Incident lifecycle and severity definitions
2) Roles & responsibilities
3) Pager and escalation policy
4) Runbook examples (runtime-api and cluster-degraded scenarios)
5) Postmortem process & template
6) On-call rotations and handover checklist
7) Game days (exercise plan)
8) Status page & customer comms templates
9) Maintenance, ownership and links

1) Incident lifecycle and severity definitions

Incident lifecycle (high-level):
1. Detect — automated alert or user report.
2. Triage — determine scope, affected customers, and severity.
3. Respond — assign roles (Incident Commander, SRE/Eng responders, Communications).
4. Mitigate — apply temporary fixes or fallbacks.
5. Restore — return service to normal SLO-compliant behavior.
6. Remediate — implement long-term fix.
7. Review — produce postmortem and track action items to closure.

Severity definitions (use consistently across tooling):
- Sev 1 (Critical): Widespread production outage or data-loss affecting ≥50% of requests or customers, severe SLO breach (availability <99.0% for the rolling hour) or safety/security incidents. Pager: immediate.
- Sev 2 (High): Major degradation (error rate >5% or p99 latency >2x SLO) for a major subset of traffic or important customers. Pager: immediate.
- Sev 3 (Medium): Partial service degradation or feature regression with workable fallback; localized to a small set of endpoints/customers. Pager: on-call notification, not always escalation.
- Sev 4 (Low): Operational problem without customer impact (alerts for visibility).

Concrete thresholds (examples):
- Errors: >3% request error rate sustained for 5 minutes -> Sev 2.
- Latency: p99 > 500ms sustained for 10 minutes -> Sev 2.
- Capacity: queue backlog > 2x baseline and growing for 5 minutes -> Sev 2.
(Owner: SRE maintains threshold tuning in /confluence/eng-sre/slo-definitions.)

2) Roles & responsibilities

Primary roles (assign at incident start):
- Incident Commander (IC): single decision-maker for incident scope, priorities, and communications cadence.
- Primary Responder(s): engineers who execute runbook steps.
- Secondary / Backup Responder: picks up if primary unavailable.
- Communications Lead (Comms): prepares external/internal updates and posts to status page & Slack.
- Subject Matter Experts (SMEs): owners of impacted services (runtime, cloud infra, DB, networking).
- Postmortem Author: collects timeline and artifacts after incident.

Responsibilities summary:
- IC ensures rapid triage, coordinates mitigation and declares incident severity.
- Responder(s) follow runbooks, gather logs, and test mitigations.
- Comms Lead issues structured updates and notifies customer-success for impacted customers.

3) Pager and escalation policy

Pager flow (default):
1. Alert triggers paging policy (PagerDuty).
2. Primary on-call receives page (30s). If unacknowledged after 3 minutes -> escalate to secondary.
3. After 7 minutes unacknowledged -> page team lead.
4. After 15 minutes, IC is paged (if not already).

Escalation rules by severity:
- Sev 1: immediate escalation to IC and on-call team lead; all-hands page if >15 min unresolved.
- Sev 2: immediate page to primary on-call + secondary backup.
- Sev 3/4: on-call notification; respond within shift.

Pager guidance:
- Acknowledge within 3 minutes if you will investigate.
- If you cannot respond, escalate immediately and add context to the PagerDuty incident.
- Use the incident channel on Slack (#inc-<service-name>) for coordination.

4) Runbook examples

A) runtime-api: high error rate (5+%)
Purpose: reduce user-facing errors and restore capacity.
Checklist / steps (ordered):
1. Triage: confirm alert in dashboards (Dashboards: "Runtime API: Errors & Latency" link).
2. Identify scope: sample logs by region/service (ELK/Kibana query) and check model-backend health.
3. Apply immediate mitigation:
   - If upstream model unavailable: switch traffic to fallback model by updating route in Runtime Router (CLI: rwin router set-route --service runtime-api --model fallback-v1).
   - If worker pool OOM/eviction: scale pool + drain problematic nodes (k8s: kubectl scale deployment/runtime-api-workers --replicas=<n>).
4. Monitor: watch for error rate dropping below 1.0% and p95 latency returning to SLO.
5. If mitigation fails in 10 minutes, escalate to IC and consider rolling rollback of latest deploy (CI: rwin deploy rollback --service runtime-api --to <commit>).
6. After restore: collect logs, export KV cache stats, and snapshot affected instances for postmortem.

Useful commands and links (placeholders):
- Dashboards: https://grafana.redwood/runtime-api
- Logs: https://kibana.redwood/logs?q=runtime-api
- Scale worker pool: kubectl scale deployment/runtime-api-workers --replicas=5 -n prod
- Rollback: rwin deploy rollback --service runtime-api --to <stable-release>

B) k8s control-plane: high CPU / pods CrashLoopBackOff
Steps:
1. Identify nodes with high CPU: kubectl top nodes.
2. Inspect pods: kubectl describe pod <pod> -n redwood-system and check events.
3. If crash due to config or image: revert configmap or image to previous known-good version.
4. If due to runaway requests: enable rate-limiting or temporarily scale replicas.
5. For resource leak: cordon & drain node, restart kubelet, and run garbage collection.
6. Post-restore: capture metrics and create ticket for capacity tuning.

Runbook best practices:
- Keep runbooks short (10-12 steps) and executable by an on-call engineer.
- Include verification steps and clear rollback criteria.
- Add owner and last-tested date at the top of each runbook.

5) Postmortem process & template

When to write a postmortem:
- All Sev 1 incidents.
- Sev 2 incidents with customer impact or repeated failures.

Timeline and ownership:
- Postmortem must be drafted within 48 hours by the Postmortem Author.
- Draft reviewed by the responder team and IC within 5 business days.
- Action items must have owners and due dates tracked in the engineering backlog.

Postmortem template (use and populate all fields):
- Title: <service> — <short summary> (Sev X)
- Summary: 2-3 sentence customer-facing summary.
- Impact: affected customers, duration, estimated % of requests impacted.
- Detection: how it was detected (alert/user report).
- Timeline: numbered minute-by-minute timeline from detection to full restore.
- Root cause: technical cause(s) and contributing factors.
- Mitigation & remediation: actions taken during incident and permanent fixes planned.
- Action items: actionable tasks, owners, and due dates.
- Lessons learned & follow-ups: operational improvements, runbook updates, test plans.
- Artifacts: links to dashboards, logs, and deployment commits.

Example action items:
- Increase default worker pool autoscaling floor to 4 for runtime-api (owner: infra-team, due: 2026-03-01).
- Add alert for cache invalidation spikes (owner: eng-sre, due: 2026-02-28).

6) On-call rotations and handover checklist

Rotation model:
- Primary on-call: 1-week rotation, Monday 08:00 -> next Monday 08:00.
- Secondary (backup): same cadence, overlapping so each week has a primary + secondary.
- On-call load: aim for no more than 1 full week per 6 weeks on average.

Handover checklist (to post in team Slack #oncall-handover):
- Current incidents and their status (open/monitoring/resolved).
- Recent deploys and rollbacks in the last 24-48 hours.
- Active maintenance windows.
- Known flapping alerts and mitigations.
- Pager duty overrides and contact list updates.

Handover script (sample message):
"Handover: @new-oncall. No open Sev1/2. Runtime-api currently healthy; last deploy 2026-02-18. Noted alerts: runtime-kv-cache spike (mitigated). Links: Grafana / Kibana. PagerDuty rota: primary @alice, backup @bob."

7) Game days (exercise plan)

Purpose: validate runbooks, tooling, and communication processes.
Cadence: quarterly full-team game days; monthly focused runbook drills.
Typical scenarios:
- Simulated model-serving outage (fallback route test).
- Large-scale spike in token generation latency.
- Region failover test and cross-region routing.
Success criteria:
- Mean time to mitigate under target (e.g., <30 minutes for simulated Sev 2).
- Clear, time-stamped incident channel messages.
- Runbook execution without >2 blockers.
Post-game day deliverables:
- Short report with failures, runbook updates, and action items.

8) Status page & customer communications templates

Status page messaging guidance:
- Be concise, transparent, and frequent for Sev1/2 (initial + regular updates every 30-60 minutes).
- Use customer-facing language; avoid internal jargon.
- Escalate to Sales & Customer Success if key accounts are affected.

Templates (use and adapt)
INITIAL (short):
Title: Incident: Degraded API availability for text generation
Message: We are investigating reports of increased errors for text generation requests. Some customers in us-west are experiencing failures. Our engineering teams are actively investigating. We will post an update within 30 minutes.

UPDATE (progress):
Title: Update: Ongoing investigation — partial mitigation applied
Message: We identified a model backend instability affecting 40% of requests for text generation. Traffic for affected routes was routed to a fallback model to reduce errors while we continue root-cause analysis. Error rates have dropped from 8% -> 1.5%. We expect further improvements in the next 30 minutes.

RESOLVED:
Title: Resolved: API availability restored
Message: Service returned to normal operation at 2026-02-20T14:12Z. Root cause: misconfiguration in model rollout pipeline that left an incompatible model active. We have deployed a permanent fix and will follow up with a postmortem with further details and actions.

Internal Slack update template:
- [SEV X] <short title>
- Impact: <who / what>
- Mitigation: <what we did>
- Action items: <1-2 immediate follow-ups>
- Links: Grafana | Kibana | Incident channel

Customer email/snippet (for customer-success):
Subject: Redwood Inference — Incident affecting text generation (Resolved)
Body: Hello <Customer name>, we experienced a partial service degradation affecting text generation from <start> to <end>. We applied a fallback and restored service. We estimate <percent> of your requests were affected. We will share a postmortem and any recommended actions. Contact support@redwood.ai for account-specific follow-up.

9) Maintenance, ownership and links

- Document owner: eng-sre (primary), eng-platform (secondary). Update cadence: review quarterly or after any Sev1/2 incident.
- Where to find runbooks: /confluence/oncall-and-incident-response/runbooks
- Where to file action items: Engineering backlog board (jira: REDWOOD-ENG-INCIDENTS).
- Useful links: Grafana, Kibana, PagerDuty, CI rollback docs, model catalog.

Appendix: runbook metadata template (to include at top of each runbook)
- Service: <service-name>
- Owner: <team/person>
- Last tested: YYYY-MM-DD
- Last updated: YYYY-MM-DD
- Contact: pager or Slack handle

Revision history:
- 2024-11-02: Initial draft (Ava Chen)

End of playbook. For questions, reach out to eng-sre@redwood.ai or post in #eng-oncall.
